instruction: Configure my touchpad so that tapping acts as a click instead of physically pressing down.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling tap-to-click on touchpad via GNOME settings. The setup disables tap-to-click, and the agent must enable it using gsettings command. The evaluator verifies the setting is enabled by reading the gsettings value.
metadata.verification: The evaluator uses existing vm_command_line getter and exact_match metric. Expected output is 'true\n' when the setting is enabled.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: executes 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.touchpad tap-to-click' which is the right command to verify tap-to-click state
Metric comparison is appropriate: exact_match correctly compares the command output with expected value 'true\n'
Expected value is semantically correct: 'true\n' is the actual output format from gsettings when tap-to-click is enabled, including the newline character
Complete coverage: instruction has one requirement (enable tap-to-click) and evaluator checks exactly that requirement
State accessibility is good: gsettings value persists after task completion, no postconfig needed
Data flow is sound: setup disables → agent enables → evaluator verifies enabled state
Edge cases handled: evaluator handles command failure cases (returns 0.0 when result is None)
